lines.text: Where is the goal? It's asked every loop, so the goal may move.
Drive To Tag uses this. Far away, it drives to the scoring spot on the field map.
Once the cameras lock on to the AprilTag, the goal jumps to the spot measured from the tag. Video three.
Drive To Piece chases a game piece the camera sees. If the piece rolls, the robot follows.
Same loop, same speed rule. Only the answer to "where is the goal" changes.
So when is the job done? Three checks, all at once.
Within two centimeters, within two degrees, and truly stopped: measured speed under five centimeters per second.
Like parking a car. You're not parked until the car stops.
A pass-through waypoint is done at its hand-over circle, still rolling.
